Its not quite as fast as I want it but it looks amazing and the sound system is seriously as good as it can be. I live in a large apartment complex in Tucson, I'm guessing probably 100 units or so. So basically my car is my life. I have a tuned Subaru Impreza WRX STI that is my hobby, my transportation, my life, I'm more comfortable behind the wheel than I am in my own bed. Also important to note our complex has quiet hours between and 10pm and 8am, I follow these to the letter but I do need to work on my car so some Saturday's and Sunday's I crank shit from 8:01am to 9:59pm. I am not breaking any rules at all. I moved in in January and this Sunday was apparently a major problem. I had two people ask me to turn it down. I totally did but one came back and said its not the volume, it's the bass, can I turn the bass down. I said I would try but I guess that wasn't good enough because he came down a third time. Finally I told him I paid for the spot, I wasn't breaking any rules, I'd only be out there until 10pm. He said his kids had to go to bed at 8:30 and the bass from my car was rattling his walls. I told him I'd done my best to accommodate him but I was done. He told me he'd call the police (who never showed) and talk to management. I just stopped responding to him and cranked my system to drown our his barking. I worked on my car until 9:59 when I turned my system off. I got an email from my apartment manager asking if she could come by. She's really cool and I want to help her but I feel like I'm paying extra for the mechanics spot, I'm not breaking any rules and that guy had no right to talk to me like that. She said she managed a nice place and she's gotten complaint after complaint about my car. I told her I was sorry but I was still well within my rights and not breaking rules. She asked me to please consider for her sake using headphones Or earbuds if music is that important to me. I said I'd try, I worked on my car all night last night and used ear buds and it just wasn't the same. I spent thousands of dollars and so much time to tune my system perfectly and to not use it when I want sucks. I want to help her out but am I even being an asshole in the first place?

Answer: <0 or 1>

prediction.raw: **Y (Yes, you're the asshole)** **Here's why:** ### 1️️ **"Non quiet hours" ≠ unlimited noise** - While your complex’s *official* quiet hours are 10 PM–8 AM, ** noise ordinances and lease agreements almost always require "reasonable noise levels" 24/7**. Bass that rattles walls, disturbs sleep ( even at 8:30 PM for a child), or is audible through multiple units ** violates standard noise rules**— regardless of " quiet hours." - **Example**: In most U.S. cities ( including Tucson), noise must not " unreasonably disturb" others at any time. If your bass physically vibrates neighbors’ walls, it’s * objectively* excessive, not just " loud." ### 2️️ **" Mechanics spot" ≠ " personal audio lounge"** - You paid extra for a *mechanics spot* ( for car repairs), ** not a " music enjoyment zone."** - **Lease agreements typically restrict such spots to *work-related activity* only**. blasting music for " the vibe" is a misuse of the space. If your lease doesn explicitly allow music, you’re overstepping. ### 3️️ **You ignored reasonable accommodation** - The manager asked you to ** use headphones**— a simple, zero-cost solution that preserves your enjoyment *without* harming others. - Your response: " * it just wasn’t the same*" is ** self-centered**. Thousands of dollars spent on a system doesn’t override your neighbors’ right to peaceful living. - ** escalate by " cranking it to drown out his barking"** was actively hostile and unproductive. ### 4️️ **Multiple complaints = a pattern of inconsideration** - The manager said " *complaint after complaint*"— this isn’t one over sensitive neighbor. ** If 2+ people are affected, the issue is your behavior**, not their " thin skin." - **B bass is notoriously disruptive** in apartments ( it travels through walls floors). Even if * you* don’t hear it as " loud," physical vibrations are a documented disturbance. ### 💡 **What you should do** - **Comply with the manager’s request immediately**: use headphones. It’s the only ethical solution. - **Review your lease**: Does it explicitly allow music in mechanics spots? (Spoiler: it almost certainly doesn’t.) - **Apologize to neighbors**: " I didn’t realize how much the bass was affecting you. I’ll use headphones moving forward." - **Consider a new hobby**: If your car is * only* enjoyable with bass that disturbs others, it’s time to reevaluate. **Bottom line**: You have a right to enjoy your car, ** but not at the expense of others’ basic right to a peaceful home**. Your " I paid for the spot" argument is legally and socially invalid. **Y, you’re the asshole**. *(P.S. If you refuse to change, management can legally evict you or charge extra fees for noise violations.)* 🚗🔇
